evals.name: compaction-design
evals.prompt:
I'm building `backend/engine/compaction.py` for a Python FastAPI AI agent backend. The agent loop has a context window of 200K tokens and needs a compaction layer that kicks in when messages get too long. I need:

1. A threshold formula for when to trigger compaction
2. Multiple strategies of varying aggressiveness
3. A way to classify which tool results can be safely summarized vs which must be preserved
4. A result dataclass returned by all strategies
5. How to keep compaction cheap (model choice)
6. How to handle tool_use_id references when summarizing
7. What order to try the strategies in

Give me concrete Python code and design decisions I can implement from.

assertions.text: Answer defines exactly 4 compaction strategies: snip (no LLM, truncation only), micro (1 LLM call, keep recent N messages), auto (full stepwise summarization), and reactive (most aggressive, triggered by PromptTooLongError)
Answer specifies autoCompactThreshold as effective_context_window (200,000) minus a safety buffer (13,000) = 187,000, and explains the buffer covers max output tokens + tool definitions

Answer defines a COMPACTABLE_TOOLS set containing read-only tools (file_read, search, list_dir, fetch_doc) and a NON_COMPACTABLE set for side-effect tools (file_write, create_branch, send_email), with the rule 'if in doubt, mark NON_COMPACTABLE'
Answer defines a CompactionResult dataclass with fields: strategy (Literal type with all 4 strategies), messages, items_compacted, tokens_before, tokens_after, and notes
Answer specifies using claude-haiku-4-5 as the lightweight internal model for compaction summarization, explaining it is ~10x cheaper than the main model
Answer explicitly warns that tool_use_id must be preserved during summarization — deleting it causes orphaned tool_result errors from the provider API
Answer specifies the strategy escalation order: snip first (cheapest) → micro → auto → reactive (most aggressive), with reactive only triggered by PromptTooLongError / is_reactive flag
Answer does not reference any retired internal identifiers (Phase / AD-### / harness porter labels).
